title: Poisson disk scatter with instance matrices
purpose: Scatter blue-noise points in a rectangle with a guaranteed minimum spacing (Bridson's algorithm), an optional mask with restarts for separate regions and density thinning, and turn them into seeded yaw and scale instance matrices for three.js InstancedMesh. Use it for forests, rocks, crowds, props and decals.

engine.name: node
engine.notes: No three.js needed: points and matrices are typed arrays to copy into InstancedMesh.instanceMatrix.array. The demo was rendered with three.js 0.186.1 in headless Chrome.

exports.name: poissonDiskPoints
exports.summary: Points with at least minDistance between any two, inside the rectangle and the mask, thinned by density; deterministic for a seed.

exports.name: toInstanceMatrices
exports.signature: toInstanceMatrices(points, options = {}) -> Float32Array (16 per point, column-major)
exports.summary: Matrices that place, spin and scale a model at each point on the XZ or XY plane.

options.name: height
options.meaning: Field size along y (z on the ground plane).

options.name: minDistance
options.meaning: Smallest allowed distance between two points.

options.name: attempts
options.meaning: Candidates tried around each active point before it retires.

options.name: mask
options.meaning: mask(x, y) truthy keeps a candidate.

options.name: density
options.meaning: density(x, y) in [0, 1] is the chance a finished point is kept.

options.name: plane
options.meaning: toInstanceMatrices: 'xz' ground plane spinning about +Y, or 'xy' spinning about +Z.

options.name: scaleJitter
options.meaning: toInstanceMatrices: scale varies by up to this fraction either way.

options.name: yawJitter
options.meaning: toInstanceMatrices: spin is uniform in [0, yawJitter).

limits: One minimum distance for the whole field: no variable radius. Density thins finished points, which keeps the spacing but loses the even blue-noise look where density is low. Restarts after the frontier stops find separate mask regions by random tries, so a very small region can be missed. The mask is a callback run for every candidate, so a slow mask slows sampling. The field is a rectangle; points lie in float32. Matrices spin about one axis with uniform scale; no tilt to a slope. Only three.js 0.186.1 was run for the demo, in headless Chrome on SwiftShader WebGL 2.
technique_references: Bridson fast Poisson disk sampling with a background grid of cell size r / sqrt(2)
Uniform sampling of the annulus [r, 2r] by area
Random sequential packing density as a plausibility band
